_readme: Copy for Tundra's choice-payoffs-v0.2 (8015554). Tokens: {catName} = the cat speaking, {sourceName} = the cat who passed the fact on (§1.4, Tundra wrote {catName}; renamed so it's not the speaker), {playerName}, {zoneName}. No pronoun tokens, no numbers. Openers have one line per sociability band, so exactly one plays. Choice 'text' is what plays after the pick.

1.3_knows_name_opener.text: "{playerName}! You came back." {catName} sounds honestly pleased. "I hoped you would."
"{playerName}. You came back." {catName} says the name carefully, as if checking it still fits.
"{playerName}." Just the name, flat, and a long look. "You came back, then."

1.4_pridemate_heard_opener.text: "Wait, you're the one {sourceName} spoke of! I wondered when I'd see you."
"You're the one {sourceName} spoke of." {catName} looks you over, comparing you to the story.
"You're the one {sourceName} spoke of." It doesn't sound like a compliment, and it doesn't sound like an insult.

opener.text: "Still walking alone? I keep thinking about that. It seems a lonely way to live."
"Still walking alone?" {catName} glances past you, as if half expecting someone this time.
"Still alone." It isn't quite a question. {catName} has noticed.

for_now.label: "For now."
for_now.text: "For now," you say. {catName} lets it rest there.

not_by_choice.label: "Not by choice."
not_by_choice.text: "Not by choice." It comes out more honest than you meant. {catName} goes quiet, and you can see the words being kept somewhere.

leave.label: Change the subject.
leave.text: You turn the talk to the weather and the prey. {catName} follows your lead without pushing.

1.5_seeking_company_gossip_opener.text: "I heard you're looking for company out there. Is that true? Because I could do with some myself."
"I heard you're looking for company out there. Is that true?"
"Word is you're looking for company." A long look. "I'm only telling you what I heard."

text.text: "Tomorrow? Yes!" {catName} doesn't even pretend to think about it. "I'll be there."
{catName} thinks it over, then nods once. "{zoneName}, tomorrow. All right."
"Maybe." {catName} looks away. "If I'm passing." It sounds more like yes than no.

say_goodbye.label: Say goodbye.
say_goodbye.text: You part ways. {catName} looks back once before the land swallows the trail.

2.2_you_came.text: {catName} is already there, and comes to meet you halfway. "You came!"
{catName} is waiting at {zoneName}, and sits up when you appear. "You came."
{catName} is there, pretending not to be waiting. "You came." A pause. "Good."

opener.text: "I waited at {zoneName}. All day." {catName} sounds more hurt than angry. "Did something happen?"
"I waited at {zoneName}." {catName} says it plainly, and waits to hear why.
"I waited at {zoneName}." {catName}'s tail flicks once. "I won't make a habit of it."

explain.label: Tell {catName} what kept you.
explain.text: You tell {catName} what kept you. {catName} listens to all of it, and some of the stiffness goes out of the moment.

repair.label: "I'm sorry. I should have come."
repair.text: "I'm sorry. I should have come." {catName} looks at you a long moment, then lets it go.

leave.label: Say nothing about it.
leave.text: You don't answer. {catName} doesn't ask again, and the silence sits between you.

opener.text: "You ate the whole thing and never looked up!" {catName} sounds more amazed than angry. "I was right there."
"You ate the whole thing and never looked up." {catName} says it lightly, but watches for your answer.
"You ate the whole thing and never looked up." {catName} hasn't forgotten a single bite.

promise_share.label: "Next time, I'll share."
promise_share.text: "Next time, I'll share." {catName}'s ears come forward. "I'll hold you to that."

my_kill.label: "It was my kill."
my_kill.text: "It was my kill." {catName} takes that in without a word, and something between you goes a little colder.

leave.label: Let it go.
leave.text: You let the remark pass. {catName} doesn't press it.
